trust.title: Who can see your data
trust.p1: Your orders, customers, suppliers and conversations are yours. Database policy isolates each company; nobody at another company can read them.

trust.title: Who can see your data, and who cannot
trust.intro: Merchandising runs on relationships: which factory makes what, at what price, for which customer. VIA Merch is built so that this stays inside your company. Every statement below is enforced in the product, not only promised.

isolation.title: Each company is isolated
isolation.body: Every record carries your company's identity and the database refuses to return it to anyone else. People at another company, and that company's agents, cannot read your orders, customers, suppliers, conversations, drafts or ledger. This is a database rule, applied on every query, not a filter in the screen.

staff.title: VIA Labs staff see nothing inside your records
staff.body: Our people can see what is needed to run the service: your company's name and plan, who its members are, which autonomy levels are set, how many agent runs and messages there were, and what they cost. They cannot open your orders, parties, conversations, drafts or ledger. The same database rule that keeps other companies out keeps us out.

support.title: Support access is granted by you, for 72 hours, on the record
support.body: When we need to look inside, for set-up or troubleshooting, we ask. An owner or manager at your company sees the request and the reason in Settings and by email, and grants or declines. A grant lasts 72 hours, can be revoked at any moment, and the request, the grant, the first opening and the revocation are written to your ledger. Without a grant, our console does not even show your customer names.

agents.title: The agents are software, and every action is logged
agents.body: Your agent reads your channels and works your records as software on our infrastructure. It drafts; a person at your company approves anything that commits money, stock or dates. Price clarification, claims and order confirmation can never be sent by an agent alone. Every agent action is a signed, append-only row on your ledger, which your managers can read and export.

mcp.title: Your own agent can work here too, under the same rules
mcp.body: A member can issue a personal token so an agent they run themselves, in any tool that speaks MCP, reads what that member can read and queues drafts and dates for a person to approve. The token is stored as a hash, expires after 90 days, can be revoked by the member or a manager, and is limited to the member's role, customers and tracks. That agent cannot send a message, approve a draft, take a sample decision or read payment details, and every call is on the run log and the ledger.

partners.title: A partner who also runs VIA Merch sees only what you share
partners.body: When a customer or supplier also runs VIA Merch, your agent and theirs can exchange status, dates, trace records and bookings. They see only the records of the orders you share with them, through a stream whose autonomy level you set, and nothing about your other customers, suppliers or prices.

models.title: The model is chosen for your region and your requirements
models.body: VIA Merch runs each company on the best model available to it, by where the company is based and what it requires. The standard profile is Anthropic's Claude models through Anthropic's API. Claude is not offered to companies based in Hong Kong or mainland China, so they run on a leading model available there, such as DeepSeek or Qwen. Where your requirements call for a particular provider or hosting region, we set that instead. The profile is fixed for your company by VIA Labs in the software, never chosen by the agent, and the same isolation, approvals and ledger apply on every profile. We only use a provider under terms where your text is used to produce the response and not to train models. Your provider is named in your agreement; if it changes, you hear from us first.

infra.title: Where your data lives
infra.body: Managed Postgres (Supabase) and application servers (Vercel) in Singapore, encrypted in transit and at rest. Secrets live in the hosting provider's vault, not in code. VIA Labs Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore company.

signin.title: Sign-in and sessions
signin.body: There are no passwords to leak. People sign in with a one-time code sent to their work email, which works once and expires in an hour. Sessions end after two hours without activity. Access is by invitation from your owner or manager; VIA Labs can invite the first owner and nobody else without your say.

yours.title: Your data stays yours
yours.body: Export your orders, parties, conversations and ledger as xlsx, csv or json at any time. When you leave, ask and we delete your company's records, and confirm in writing when it is done.

desk.title: The support desk is addressed to us
desk.body: A conversation you open at the support desk is a message to VIA Labs, so our staff read it, along with any screenshot you attach. The support agent answers from the product guide and can see only your role, your tracks, your add-ons and the state of your connections. It cannot read your orders, customers, suppliers, conversations, drafts, ledger or bank details, and it cannot change anything in your workspace. Opening and closing a ticket is written to your ledger.

switchboard.title: Sits on top of the tools you already use.
switchboard.lede: Mira is the operator. She patches what arrives in one tool through to where it has to go next, and asks you before anything goes out. Every connection stays on the board, so you can see it all.
switchboard.note: Hover or tap a socket to see what Mira does there; click one to watch it in use. Scenes are examples. The full list of connectors scrolls underneath.

events.e6: A PO is approved in SAP Business One. Mira sends it to the factory on WhatsApp, in Bangla.
events.e7: A factory audit in Sedex expires before shipment. Mira drafts the reminder in Outlook.
events.e8: A factory in Vietnam asks for an inline QC slot on Zalo. Mira books it in Inspectorio.

esg.title: ESG & compliance
esg.sub: Every compliance requirement that reaches the company, from lenders, customers, certifiers, auditors and authorities, turned into dated work for the right people and the right suppliers. Figures, documents and certificates are gathered and checked, then compiled into the report back.
esg.addonTitle: Every compliance requirement, carried down to the people and suppliers who do the work
esg.addonP1: Bank covenants, brand codes of conduct, audits and corrective actions, certificates and licences, test reports and transaction certificates per order, market rules in the EU and US. They reach the owner or the account manager, then get lost, misread or forgotten on the way to the people who do the work. VIA Merch carries each requirement down to the person or supplier responsible, reminds them in good time, gathers the evidence and prepares the report back.
esg.how1: Start from a template (bank ESAP, code of conduct, BSCI, WRAP, OEKO-TEX, GOTS, ZDHC, EU and US market rules, local licences) or upload the document itself. The agent reads every obligation; you check it before anything is saved.
esg.how2: Each requirement has an owner, the evidence that proves it, and when it falls due: every period, for every matching order at a production milestone, or before a certificate or licence expires. It can apply to the company or to every matching supplier.
esg.how3: Tasks are created ahead of each due date. Owners are emailed when the lead time starts, a week before and the day before, and the agent queues requests to suppliers for approval.
esg.how4: Figures and evidence are versioned and checked by a compliance lead. The agent drafts the report; an owner or manager approves it; you download or print it for the bank.
